Subject: Dedicated capacity guarantees — throughput & queueing questions

Hi Irene / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving toward an internal approval for Reserved GPUs but need clarity on how Redwood's dedicated capacity warranty maps to our production patterns before procurement signs off. A few concrete items: 

- Throughput guarantees: can you confirm how you measure the "throughput floor"? Do you guarantee token/sec, or a token-hour availability per reserved unit?
- Tail latency: we currently need 95th < 150ms for our call routing small-model flows and 99th < 350ms for larger NLU models — does the dedicated SLA cover both or only a typical aggregate?
- Queueing behavior during peaks: if batch jobs run and cause preemption, how are interactive requests prioritized? Any carveouts?
- Credits: how are credits calculated if we observe a capacity shortfall during our peak campaign (we expect ~3x baseline for 10 days in mid-Oct)?

I've attached a short sample of our hourly spikes (usage-spike-sample.csv). Procurement will need a draft appendix for our legal team that spells out metrics and crediting so they can include it in the PO.

Can we get a short written response and an updated appendix by next Wednesday (10/6)? If useful, we can jump on a 30-min call.

--
Sanjay Rao
Head of Engineering, Borealis Health
Sanjay.Rao@borealishealth.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guarantees — throughput & queueing questions

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear list and the sample file.

Short answers up front, with details below and an attached SLA appendix draft (sla-appendix-draft.docx) for procurement: 

1) Throughput measurement: we map "reservation units" to GPU reservation-hours and report a ReservedTokenSeconds metric. A reservation unit = 1 reserved GPU slot configured for your chosen SKU (e.g., rdx-p4d). The throughput floor is expressed as a monthly entitlement of ReservedTokenSeconds. Operationally we monitor served token-seconds per hour; a shortfall is when served < committed for a rolling hour window.

2) Latency coverage: the dedicated SLA covers latency SLOs per request class (interactive vs batch). We'll propose 95th and 99th percentile SLOs per model class in the appendix; the dedicated pool will prioritize interactive lanes to meet your 95th SLO.

3) Queueing & prioritization: we support soft-priority lanes — interactive requests get a high-priority queue and are served from a dedicated fraction of the pool (inflight slots). Batch jobs run in preemptible lanes and can be evicted under sustained contention; batch eviction is signaled and we publish eviction traces.

4) Crediting: our standard approach is pro-rata monthly credit based on token-second shortfall during the billing period; see the example in the appendix. We can tailor the crediting to a throughput-floor model for enterprise commits (example: TokensShort / ReservedTokenSeconds * CommitValue).

Action items: Ben, can you confirm commercial language for credits and whether we can offer a temporary "peak bridge" (one-time buffer of reservation units) for the 10/15–10/22 window? Lauren, will you coordinate procurement contacts and confirm the legal placeholders we need?

I've attached redwood-sla-proposal-v2.pdf (proposal that explains measurement artifacts) and the appendix draft. Happy to iterate. If helpful, propose a 30-min slot Monday 10/4 10:00–10:30 PT.

Best,
Irene
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

(attachments: redwood-sla-proposal-v2.pdf (pdf), sla-appendix-draft.docx (docx))

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@borealishealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guarantees — throughput & queueing questions

Sanjay — appreciate the context. A few commercial / practical clarifications that usually help procurement sign off quickly: 

1) Crediting formula (worked example):
   - Define ReservedTokenSeconds (RTS) = reserved_units * gpu_seconds_per_unit * expected_tokens_per_second
   - ObservedServedTokenSeconds (OSTS) = sum over billing period of served token-seconds for your tenant
   - ShortfallRatio = max(0, 1 - (OSTS / RTS))
   - Credit = ShortfallRatio * MonthlyCommitValue

   Example: RTS = 10M token-seconds/month, OSTS = 9.2M => ShortfallRatio = 0.08 => Credit = 8% of the monthly reserved commitment. This stays within our standard accounting flows and is straightforward for finance.

2) Temporary peak bridge: we can provision a one-time pool buffer of up to 20% reserved units for up to 14 days at an agreed uplift. That avoids invoking credits for predictable short campaigns. We mark the buffer as "ephemeral reservation" and it will be billed as a one-off committed uplift.

3) Queueing & eviction windows: we propose a 120s preemption grace period for batch jobs — meaning when contention hits, batch in-flight requests have 120s to finish before eviction; interactive requests are routed to the high-priority queue which consumes up to X% of the pool (to be set per appendix).

4) Measurement artifacts: we'll include a per-hour CSV dump of ReservedTokenSeconds, ObservedServedTokenSeconds, and per-request latency percentiles so Borealis' SREs can independently verify.

If that model looks sensible, we can add the numeric parameters to the appendix and route to legal. Irene, I'll sync the uplift pricing and produce a short commercial addendum.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales — Enterprise

All — attaching the updated appendix (sla-appendix-draft.docx) and a short summary of changes for Borealis procurement: 

Summary of updates:
- Measurement: ReservedTokenSeconds defined and example calculations included.
- Latency: Interactive (small models) 95th <= 150ms, 99th <= 300ms; Large NLU 95th <= 250ms, 99th <= 400ms (values can be tuned per model list).
- Priority lanes: default high-priority allocation set to 35% of the dedicated pool; batch lane eviction grace = 120s.
- Crediting: pro-rata monthly credit using the ShortfallRatio formula (worked example added).
- Peak bridge: one-time ephemeral reservation up to 20% of committed units for up to 14 days; uplift = +18% of monthly reserved cost (Ben — please confirm final uplift).
- Observability: hourly CSV export (ReservedTokenSeconds, ObservedServedTokenSeconds, pctiles) + request-level traces on demand for audit.

Next steps:
1) Ben: confirm uplift number for the peak bridge and I will insert the commercial sentence into the appendix.
2) Lauren: if procurement confirms 10/15–10/22 for their campaign, we'll create the ephemeral reservation and route the DocuSign addendum to their procurement contact.
3) Sanjay: please reply with any model-class-specific latency tweaks — otherwise I'll push the current numbers into the DocuSign draft.

If we agree, I'll upload the DocuSign draft to the related link and notify procurement.

Thanks everyone —
